config.enabled.name: Enable SDV-Radiance
config.enabled.tooltip: Master switch for the whole post-processing pipeline.
config.preset.hint: Tip: presets and your saved custom looks live in the on-screen tuner (open with the tuner hotkey, default F6). It previews live and always stays in sync.
config.preset.name: Quick preset
config.preset.tooltip: Apply a ready-made look. This overwrites the bloom and color-grading settings below; reopen the menu to see the updated values.
config.togglekey.name: Toggle effects on/off
config.togglekey.tooltip: Instantly turn the whole post-processing stack on or off (quick A/B compare while playing).
config.tunerkey.name: Open live tuner
config.tunerkey.tooltip: Open the on-screen tuner overlay to adjust the look while seeing the scene live.
tuner.title: SDV-Radiance Tuner
tuner.hint: Drag = preview  •  wheel = scroll  •  right-click a look = delete  •  Esc = save
config.bloom.enabled.name: Enable bloom
config.bloom.enabled.tooltip: Glow around bright areas such as lamps and sunlight.
config.bloom.threshold.name: Bloom threshold
config.bloom.intensity.name: Bloom intensity
config.colorgrade.enabled.name: Enable color grading
config.colorgrade.enabled.tooltip: Cinematic tone/palette adjustment (done in linear color space).
config.colorgrade.auto.name: Auto mood (time / weather / season)
config.colorgrade.auto.tooltip: Automatically shift warmth and saturation: warm at sunset, cool at night, cooler and desaturated in rain/snow, with a seasonal bias.
config.colorgrade.strength.name: Strength
config.colorgrade.contrast.name: Contrast
config.colorgrade.saturation.name: Saturation
config.colorgrade.temperature.name: Temperature (warm / cool)
config.colorgrade.temperature.tooltip: Negative = cooler/bluer, positive = warmer/oranger. Added on top of the auto mood.
config.colorgrade.brightness.name: Brightness
config.colorgrade.tonemap.name: Filmic tone mapping (ACES)
config.colorgrade.tonemap.tooltip: Off by default. The frame is already low-dynamic-range, so this mainly helps when Brightness is pushed above 1 — otherwise it can look muddy.
config.colorgrade.bluelight.name: Blue-light filter
config.colorgrade.bluelight.tooltip: Eye-comfort warm shift: cuts blue and lifts red a touch, like a night-light mode. 0 = off. Works even with color grading turned off.
config.godrays.enabled.name: Enable god rays
config.godrays.enabled.tooltip: Shafts of light spreading out from LAMPS, torches and fires, strongest in a dark room or after dusk. Shafts from the sun are the separate switch below, and each works without the other.
config.godrays.intensity.name: Intensity
config.godrays.threshold.name: Light threshold
config.godrays.density.name: Ray length
config.fog.enabled.name: Enable day fog
config.fog.enabled.tooltip: Drifting screen-space mist during the day; fades out over dusk.
config.fog.nightmist.name: Enable night mist
config.fog.nightmist.tooltip: Sparse blue wisps that drift by after dusk (outdoors, clear weather). Fades in as day fog fades out.
config.fog.nightmistdensity.name: Night mist intensity
config.fog.nightmistcoverage.name: Night mist amount
config.fog.nightmistspeed.name: Night mist drift speed
config.fog.coverage.name: Fog amount
config.fog.coverage.tooltip: How much of the screen the wisps occupy.
config.fog.density.tooltip: How strongly each wisp tints the scene.
config.fog.density.name: Density
config.fog.scale.name: Mist scale
config.fog.speed.name: Drift speed
tuner.waterhere.always: Water here: always on (outdoor / level water)
config.tiltshift.enabled.name: Enable tilt-shift
config.tiltshift.enabled.tooltip: Keep a sharp band across the middle and blur the top and bottom (fake miniature / depth-of-field look).
config.tiltshift.mode.name: Focus shape
config.tiltshift.mode.tooltip: Bands = sharp middle strip, blurred top & bottom. Radial = sharp circle around the player, blurred outward.
config.tiltshift.radius.name: Sharp circle size (radial)
config.tiltshift.radius.tooltip: Radial mode only: how big the in-focus circle around the player is before it blurs outward.
config.tiltshift.feather.name: Edge softness
config.tiltshift.feather.tooltip: How gradually the image eases from sharp to blurred. Higher is softer, removing the hard band edge.
config.tiltshift.strength.name: Blur strength
config.tiltshift.top.name: Top blur amount
config.tiltshift.bottom.name: Bottom blur amount
config.cloudshadow.hidevanilla.name: Hide vanilla cloud shadows
config.cloudshadow.hidevanilla.tooltip: Remove the base game's drifting Cloud-critter shadows (so only this mod's cloud shadows show).
config.cloudshadow.enabled.name: Enable cloud shadows
config.cloudshadow.enabled.tooltip: Soft shadows of drifting clouds moving across the ground (outdoors only).
config.cloudshadow.opacity.name: Opacity
config.cloudshadow.coverage.name: Coverage
config.cloudshadow.scale.name: Cloud size
config.cloudshadow.count.name: Cloud count
config.cloudshadow.count.tooltip: How many separate cloud banks share the screen - low = a few big drifting banks, high = many small puffs.
config.cloudshadow.speed.name: Drift speed
config.water.enabled.name: Enable water shimmer
config.water.enabled.tooltip: Gentle refraction ripple and sparkle applied only to water tiles (the game already animates the water, so this is subtle). Experimental.
config.water.strength.name: Ripple strength
config.water.speed.name: Ripple speed
config.water.sparkle.name: Sparkle
config.water.sparkledensity.name: Sparkle amount
config.water.sparkledensity.tooltip: How many glints dot the water (their size follows along). 1.0 = the original dense look; lower = calmer surface.
config.water.reflection.name: Water reflection
config.water.reflection.tooltip: Faintly mirror the scene just above the surface down onto the water for a wet, reflective sheen. Subtle by design. Experimental.
config.water.reflectstrength.name: Reflection strength
config.water.indoors.name: Water effect indoors
config.water.indoors.tooltip: Apply the water effect inside building interiors (farmhouse, cabins, house mods). Turn off if a house/interior mod has decorative water you don't want rippling. Real level water always keeps the effect: caves, mines, the sewer, and the bathhouse hot spring.
config.vignette.enabled.name: Enable vignette
config.vignette.enabled.tooltip: Darken the screen edges for a cinematic frame.
config.vignette.strength.name: Vignette strength
config.ca.enabled.name: Enable chromatic aberration
config.ca.enabled.tooltip: Subtle color fringing toward the edges, like a camera lens. Keep it low on pixel art.
config.ca.strength.name: Aberration strength
config.lighting.flood.name: Flood GI lighting
config.lighting.flood.tooltip: Occlusion-aware global illumination: real light sources and skylight flood across the map tile-by-tile, so canopies and buildings cast soft shade, lamps pool warm coloured light around corners, and windows spill light at night. Replaces the classic dynamic lighting below when enabled.
config.lighting.floodstrength.name: Flood lighting strength
config.lighting.floodstrength.tooltip: How strongly the flood lightmap shades the scene. Lower keeps the vanilla look with a hint of shading.
config.lighting.floodshadow.name: Per-light shadow strength
config.lighting.floodshadow.tooltip: How dark it gets where a wall, tree, or character blocks a lamp's light. Every light source casts its own soft shadows.
config.lighting.enabled.name: Enable dynamic lighting
config.lighting.enabled.tooltip: Darken flat/unlit areas and pool warm light around real light sources (lamps, torches, fireplaces). Makes dark places read dark and lit places read bright, with soft falloff.
config.lighting.indoor.name: Indoor darkness
config.lighting.indoor.tooltip: How much to darken interiors. The game leaves most rooms flat and fully bright; this brings back shadow so lamps actually matter. 0 = off.
config.lighting.night.name: Extra night darkness
config.lighting.night.tooltip: How dark the world gets after nightfall, outdoors and in rooms we light ourselves. The moonlit ground leans cool and quiet while lamps and fires keep their full colour, so deeper night also means the lights matter more.
config.lighting.warmth.name: Light warmth
config.lighting.boost.name: Light brightness
config.lighting.radius.name: Light radius scale
config.lighting.shadows.name: Cast shadows
config.lighting.shadows.tooltip: Tall/solid tiles (walls, structures) block light and cast soft shadows away from each light source. Experimental.
config.lighting.shadowstrength.name: Shadow strength
config.lighting.windoweffects.name: Window effects
config.lighting.windoweffects.tooltip: Everything this mod does with windows, in one switch: daylight coming into a room, and the warm glow on house windows outdoors after dark. Turn it off if another mod handles your windows. Rooms still darken and brighten through the day either way.
config.lighting.windowbeam.name: Window beam and glass
config.lighting.windowbeam.tooltip: The part of window daylight you can see: lit glass, a beam leaning with the sun, and the patch of sun it lays on the floor. Turn this off if another window mod already draws these. The room still fills with daylight from its windows either way: that half is lighting rather than art, and a mod painting window pictures cannot do it for you.
config.shadows.enabled.name: Enable directional shadows
config.shadows.enabled.tooltip: Cast a soft, sheared silhouette of each character away from the sun, leaning by time of day (outdoors, daytime, clear weather only). Experimental.
config.shadows.strength.name: Shadow strength
config.shadows.length.name: Shadow length
config.shadows.blur.name: Edge softness
config.shadows.objects.name: Shadows for trees & bushes
config.shadows.objects.tooltip: Also cast leaning shadows from trees and bushes, not just characters.
config.shadows.casts.name: Shadows per character
config.shadows.casts.tooltip: How many lights a character casts a shadow from indoors and after dark, nearest first. Also a performance setting: each one is a full shadow drawn for that character, so 1 costs a third of 3 in a room full of lamps. The sun outdoors is one light and is not affected.
config.shadows.heightdrop.name: Building & ledge shadows
config.shadows.heightdrop.tooltip: Project ground shadows from walls, buildings, and ledges (requires the Height Framework mod).
config.shadows.heightlength.name: Building shadow length
config.camera.mode.name: Camera mode
config.camera.mode.tooltip: Off = vanilla snap. Smooth = ease toward the player while moving, snap crisply when you stop.
config.smoothcam.speed.name: Follow speed
config.smoothcam.speed.tooltip: Smooth mode only. How quickly the camera catches up while moving. Lower = smoother/more trailing; 1.0 = instant.
config.renderscale.name: Effect resolution
config.renderscale.tooltip: Resolution the effects are computed at, as a fraction of your window. The game world is always drawn at full size; only the effects use a smaller image, so lowering this costs much less GPU work (0.5 is about a quarter). 1.0 = native. 0.5 is the cleanest lower setting for pixel art; values in between are softer and can shimmer slightly while the camera moves.
config.rendersharpness.name: Upscale sharpening
config.rendersharpness.tooltip: How much sharpening is applied while scaling the effects back up to your window. 0 turns it off, 1 is the tuned default (it already gets stronger as you lower the effect resolution), and higher is crisper still. Has no effect at 1.0 effect resolution, because nothing is being scaled up.
tuner.desc.looks: Pick a ready-made look, or save your own.
tuner.desc.perf: How much work the effects do. Lower it if the game stutters.
tuner.desc.colorgrade: The overall colour of the picture: warmth, contrast, richness.
tuner.desc.bloom: Bright things glow and bleed a little light into what is around them.
tuner.desc.lens: Camera-lens touches: blurred edges, darkened corners, colour fringing.
tuner.desc.lighting: How dark rooms and nights get, and how lamps pool light.
tuner.desc.shadows: Shadows cast by people, animals and objects, following the sun.
tuner.desc.godrays: Visible shafts of light, from lamps and fires or slanting down from the sun.
tuner.desc.water: Ripples, sparkle and reflections on every water surface.
tuner.desc.cloudshadow: Cloud shadows drifting slowly across the ground outdoors.
tuner.desc.fog: Daytime fog and the thin mist that gathers at night.
tuner.desc.camera: How the camera follows you as you walk.
tuner.desc.debug: Troubleshooting only. Leave this off unless you are reporting a problem.
config.debug.name: Debug logging
config.debug.tooltip: Log render-pipeline info to the SMAPI console to help troubleshoot.
config.wip.text:
These effects are planned but not implemented yet, so they have no settings here:
- High-quality texture upscaling
Each effect will get its own options as it lands.
config.water.reflstyle.name: Reflection look
config.water.reflstyle.tooltip: How much the water's own movement is allowed to break up what it is reflecting. Still water keeps the surface rippling but the image in it readable; Choppy breaks it up and reads deeper. This is separate from the ripple strength, so calming a reflection no longer means flattening the water.
help.reflstyle.still: The surface keeps rippling, but the reflection in it barely moves and sits lighter, so you can read what is being reflected. Useful in rain, where the game makes the water half again as choppy on its own.
help.reflstyle.natural: The reflection moves with the surface, which is what this mod has always shipped.
help.reflstyle.choppy: The reflection is broken up by the water and reads deeper. For open sea and weather.
tuner.windowcompat: Off: another window mod is drawing its own beam.
//: Plain-language notes shown when the pointer rests on a control in the on-screen tuner.
help.master: Turns every effect in this mod on or off at once. Nothing here touches your save.
help.colorgrade: Changes the colours of the whole picture: contrast, how strong colours are, and whether the light reads warm or cool. Off by default, so what you see is the game's own colour.
help.automood: Lets the colour settings drift with the time of day and the weather instead of staying fixed.
help.contrast: How far apart the darks and the brights are. Above 1 deepens shadows and brightens highlights; below 1 flattens the picture.
help.saturation: How strong the colours are. 0 is black and white, 1 is unchanged, above 1 is more vivid.
help.temperature: Warm or cool. To the right the picture goes orange, like late afternoon; to the left it goes blue, like an overcast day.
help.tonemap: Rolls the very brightest areas off gently instead of letting them clip to flat white.
help.bluelight: Takes some blue out of the picture, the way a night-time screen filter does. Meant for comfort, not for looks.
help.bloom: Bright things bleed a soft glow into what is around them, the way a lamp does through a camera lens.
help.bloomthreshold: How bright a pixel has to be before it starts to glow. Raise it if too much of the screen is glowing.
help.shadows: Every character, tree and object casts a shadow of its own shape, leaning away from the sun.
help.shadowlength: How far a shadow reaches. The sun's height still decides it, so shadows are long at dawn and short at noon whatever you set here.
help.shadowblur: How soft the edge of a shadow is. 0 is a hard edge; higher is a fuzzy one, like an overcast day.
help.shadowcasts: How many nearby lamps may each throw their own shadow of one character at night. More lamps means more shadows and more work for your machine.
help.shadowobjects: Whether trees, fences, crops and furniture cast shadows too, or only people and animals.
help.lighting: The night and indoor lighting: how dark a room gets and how lamps light it back up.
help.lightindoor: How dark a room is when nothing is lighting it. Higher is darker.
help.lightnight: How dark the night is, outdoors and in. Deeper night is cooler and quieter, and makes every lamp and fire count for more.
help.lightwarmth: How orange lamplight is. At 0 a lamp is white; to the right it reads like a candle.
help.lightboost: How bright each lamp burns. This is the one to raise if the night is too dark to walk in.
help.lightradius: How wide a pool of light each lamp throws.
help.lightshadows: Whether the light from a lamp is blocked by walls and furniture instead of passing through them.
help.floodgi: Bounced light. Light that lands on a floor or a wall spills onto what is beside it, so a lit corner lifts the whole area a little. GI is the usual name for this.
help.floodstrength: How far bounced light spreads. This is the contrast between a lit part of a room and an unlit one, not the overall brightness.
help.floodshadow: How dark the areas that bounced light cannot reach become.
help.windoweffects: Daylight coming in through windows: the glow on the glass and the light it throws into the room.
help.windowbeam: The visible shaft of light on the floor under a window. Turned off on its own if another window mod is drawing one.
help.godrays: Shafts of light spreading out from LAMPS, torches and fires. Off by default. A dark room or a lamplit street at night is where to look. Sun shafts are the separate switch below.
help.godraysthreshold: How bright something has to be before it throws rays. Lower it if nothing is casting any; raise it if pale walls and snow are.
help.godraysdensity: How solid the lamp shafts look, and how far the sun's dapple stretches from the trees that cast it.
help.cloudshadow: Shadows of clouds drifting across the ground on a sunny day.
help.cloudcoverage: How much of the ground is under a cloud at any moment.
help.cloudcount: Few big clouds or many small ones.
help.fog: Drifting mist over the world. Heaviest in the early morning and in the right weather.
help.fognightmist: A separate, thinner mist that comes out after dark.
help.water: Everything the mod does to water: movement, sparkle, and reflections.
help.waterstrength: How strongly the surface moves. Lower it if the ripple is distracting.
help.watersparkle: The glints of light on the surface.
help.waterreflection: Water mirrors what stands beside it. Only what is on your screen can be reflected, so something far off the top of the screen has nothing to mirror yet.
help.waterindoors: Whether indoor water, such as a tub or a fish tank, gets the effect too.
help.tiltshift: Blurs the top and bottom of the screen and keeps the middle sharp, which makes the world look like a small model. Turn it off for an evenly sharp picture.
help.tiltfeather: How gradually the blur comes on at the edge of the sharp area.
help.tilttop: How much of the top of the screen is blurred.
help.tiltbottom: How much of the bottom of the screen is blurred.
help.vignette: Darkens the corners of the screen, the way a camera lens does, so the eye settles in the middle.
help.ca: Splits colour slightly apart towards the corners of the screen, the way a real lens does. The middle of the screen is never affected. Aberration is the camera term for it.
config.godrays.sun.name: Sun shafts
config.godrays.sun.tooltip: Sunlight falling on the ground where a canopy lets it through: bright banded patches leaning with the time of day, cut by trees and buildings, gone under an overcast sky. This is dappled light on the ground, not a beam hanging in the air - denser and hazier on a foggy morning, otherwise mostly a brightening of what it lands on. Forests and treelines show it best; open ground is lit evenly and shows none. Independent of the lamp shafts switch.
help.godrayssun: Sunlight falling through gaps in a canopy, as dappled patches ON THE GROUND rather than a beam hanging in the air. Leans with the time of day and gets denser in fog. Look at a forest floor or a treeline; open ground is lit evenly and shows none. Works on its own, without the lamp switch.
